question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=5x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi /10$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi /2$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /10}4\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
